findings.where: Where we're starting: the border on all three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), at both widths
findings.fault: Each card has a thick, saturated purple border. Purple is not in the palette and has no job in it. The rules give cards a thin sand-border edge, so these are the loudest outlines on the page, in a hue seen nowhere else on it.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brand sheet says every colour has exactly one job and cards take a 1–1.5px sand-border. A visitor would object too: a purple frame on a turquoise, sand and ink page looks like a different site's part or a browser default, not like Manta.

findings.where: Where we're starting: the resting shadow under all three destination cards, at both widths
findings.fault: The cards sit at rest under a wide, heavy shadow, on top of a strong border. The parts map shows the cards are static and none of them is a link. So the shadow and the white raised card both promise a tap that does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone who taps Canggu expecting its guide, and nothing happens. The founder too: the rules file says 'nothing sits at rest under a heavy shadow' and 'white means elevated and tappable, always'. The house rules say a static part never takes a shadow, and a resting element never takes both a border and a wide soft shadow.

findings.where: Hero: the coral 'Email … for launch news' button and the 'Explore destinations' outline button below it
findings.fault: The two hero buttons use two unrelated shape systems. The coral one is a full capsule, but the control radius is 8px. The outline one has square corners and a see-through ground, but the outline button is specified as a white surface with an 8px radius. Two buttons stacked as a pair look like they come from different kits.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because DESIGN.md fixes 8px for controls and a white ground for outline buttons. A careful visitor would also notice that the first thing they see doesn't match itself, which undercuts the 'more craft' promise.
